Commercialization Of Robotic Vascular Imaging Platform By Amit Chowdhry Today at 9:52 AM Vexev has raised $6 million in new funding to advance FDA regulatory activities and accelerate U\.S\. commercialization of VxWave, its AI-powered robotic vascular ultrasound platform\. The new financing brings the Australian medical robotics company’s total funding to $19 million\. Existing investors Blackbird Ventures, Neotribe Ventures, Startmate, and Horizon participated alongside new investors TreeArc Investment Group, TEN13, Bioshore Ventures, and Alumni Ventures\. VxWave combines robotics, AI, and ultrasound imaging to automate vascular ultrasound acquisition\. The platform is initially being developed for upper-limb imaging with an initial focus on dialysis vascular access, where patients require frequent monitoring\. The company believes autonomous imaging could reduce reliance on specialist operators while making vascular imaging more consistent and accessible\. Music Ally wrote about Swedish startup Corite when it launched last year as the latest way for artists to make money by selling off stakes in their songs to fans\. In its first month of operation, it raised $24k in fan-funding for its first crop of artists\. Now the company has been raising some funding of its own: a seed investment round from a mixture of institutional investors and music industry figures – including artist Danny Saucedo and manager Tomas Lööw\. Corite hasn’t said how much the seed round is worth, but it did provide an update on its business: it has run more than 40 artist campaigns so far in its Swedish pilot, raising more than $40k\. The new funding comes as Corite launches its platform across Europe, opening up to artists beyond its homeland at a time when many are looking for new income streams amid the collapse of live revenues\. “Through Corite artists can fund and release music with the backing of the fans – from the bedroom, kitchen or studio,” said CEO Mattias Tengblad\.

Ropedia, a Singapore start-up that supplies training data for robots and physical artificial intelligence systems, has raised US$22 million \($28\.4 million\) in a pre-Series A funding round\. It did not identify the investors in the latest round, saying only that it was led by venture firms with experience in AI, deep technology and infrastructure in Southeast Asia\. The deal brings its total funding to US$30 million\. An earlier round included investors and individuals connected to Google, Andreessen Horowitz, Nvidia and Amazon, according to the company\. Ropedia's proprietary wearable devices record first-person video, depth, movement and audio as people carry out physical tasks\. The company processes that information into training material for developers seeking to teach robots how to perform tasks in real-world settings\.
